narrative.text: The Spanish-language cover of WHO's Classification of digital interventions, services and applications in health, version 2.0, described as a shared language for the uses of digital technology in health.

A Spanish-language overview chart of the full classification, listing all digital health intervention categories and sub-interventions for people, health care providers, health management and support personnel, and data services. Groups shown include targeted and on-demand communication, personal health tracking, decision support, referral coordination, supply management, and data exchange and interoperability. The layout reads as a dense one-page map of numbered codes.
The Spanish-language inner title page of the classification of digital interventions, services and applications in health, second edition.
The Spanish-language copyright and cataloguing page, giving ISBNs, the English original title, licence terms and disclaimers.
The Spanish-language table of contents, listing the executive summary, an explanation of the classification, health system challenges, intervention groups for different users, and an annex.
Spanish-language acknowledgements naming the WHO Digital Health and Innovation staff who coordinated the update and the classifications advisory committee, and thanking funders such as USAID and CDC.

A Spanish-language executive summary defining digital health and noting the rapid pace of innovation, which calls for a common language to describe digital interventions. It states that the classification is organised around three axes: interventions, health system challenges and types of services and applications.

Lists in Spanish the main changes in this edition, such as calling clients "persons", more neutral language for varied health systems, added synonyms and new intervention categories. It then reproduces the full overview of numbered digital health interventions by user group. The list covers areas from person-centred communication and consent management to provider decision support, health system management and data services.

Explains in Spanish what the classification of digital health interventions, services and applications is: a framework that categorises how digital and mobile technologies address the needs of people and health systems. It describes the intended users and the aim of a simplified common language between health and technology communities.

Describes in Spanish current uses of the first edition, such as national digital asset inventories, investment planning, regulation, training and evaluation, and restates the three axes of the classification.

Explains in Spanish that each intervention comes with synonyms and illustrative examples, and lists the five groupings of service and application types, stressing that linking interventions to these types supports interoperability.

A Spanish-language figure linking health system challenges, digital health interventions and types of digital services and applications, illustrated with intervention codes for stock management, decision support and data aggregation.

Presents Spanish-language case studies showing how to use the classification, such as choosing digital interventions to close an information gap that leaves newborns unvaccinated, and mapping interventions in a national digital health inventory.
Lists in Spanish related WHO documents such as the digital health guideline and investment guides, defines key terms such as digital health intervention, and gives references.
A Spanish-language page containing only the running labels for the classification's user groups.
A Spanish-language section divider titled Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health.
Introduces in Spanish the framework of health system challenges, which helps programme planners identify specific bottlenecks before selecting suitable digital interventions.
A Spanish-language list of health system challenges grouped under headings such as information, availability, quality, acceptability, utilisation, efficiency, cost, accountability and equity.
Introduces in Spanish the group of digital health interventions for people, meaning members of the public who use health services and their caregivers.

A Spanish-language list of the digital health interventions for people, including targeted and untargeted communication, peer communication, personal health tracking, citizen reporting, on-demand information, financial transactions and consent management.
Describes in Spanish the interventions for people, starting with targeted communication, with definitions, synonyms and illustrative project examples such as twice-weekly calls to new mothers.

Continues the Spanish-language descriptions with targeted alerts and reminders, such as SMS appointment reminders for mothers, and untargeted mass communication, such as Ebola warning messages sent in Senegal.

Describes in Spanish peer group communication for people, such as mobile support groups for adolescents with HIV, and personal health tracking through apps, sensors and records, with a fertility tracking example.

Describes in Spanish people's access to verifiable documentation of their health status, such as digital certificates, and citizen-based reporting, with an example of reporting suspected Ebola cases by SMS.

Describes in Spanish on-demand health information for people through websites, hotlines and apps, simulated human-like conversations, and personal health financing transactions such as vouchers and payments.
Describes in Spanish digital health incentives for people, such as cash transfers linked to child vaccination, and person-centred consent management for sharing health records.
Introduces in Spanish the group of digital health interventions for health care providers, the health workers who deliver health interventions.

A Spanish-language list of digital health interventions for health care providers, such as identification and registration, health records, decision support, telemedicine, referral coordination, scheduling, training and prescription management.
Begins the Spanish-language descriptions of interventions for health care providers with identification and registration of people, including biometric identification by community health workers.
Describes in Spanish person-centred digital health records used to track health status and services over time, including registries and case management, with illustrative examples.
Describes in Spanish decision support for health care providers, such as protocol-based alerts, checklists and screening tools, with an example of detecting pregnancy complications.

Describes the telemedicine category of WHO's Classification of digital interventions, services and applications in health (Spanish edition), covering remote consultations between people and providers and remote monitoring of health or diagnostic data. Each subcategory lists related terms and a real-world example, such as health hotlines, body sensor networks and teledermatology.

Describes digital interventions for communication among health care providers, supervisors and managers, such as SMS links between ministries and health workers and performance feedback. Examples include a call centre giving weekly feedback to community nutrition workers and messaging during emergency response.

Covers peer groups for health care providers and AI-generated tailored content, such as chatbots drafting replies for providers to edit. It then describes referral coordination, including emergency response and transport and referrals between health and social services.

Describes digital tools for scheduling and planning health care providers' work, such as identifying people due for services, automated appointments and task prioritization. It also covers provider training tools, with an example of an app sending quiz notifications to refresh workers' knowledge.

Describes digital interventions for prescription and medication management, including tracking prescriptions, monitoring medication adherence through smart pill bottles and reporting adverse drug effects. It also begins the laboratory and diagnostics category, with an example of SMS notification of test results.

Continues the laboratory and diagnostics category, covering transmission of diagnostic orders, results from devices attached to digital tools such as mobile phone microscopy, and tracking of blood donations and samples. It also mentions digital payments to health care providers.
Introduces the group of digital health interventions aimed at health system managers and support personnel, who administer and oversee health systems.

A one-page overview of the classification's interventions for health system managers, listing categories such as human resource management, supply chain, civil registration, health financing, equipment and asset management and facility management with their subcategories.

Begins describing interventions for health system managers, starting with human resource management, such as registries of health workers and monitoring of their performance. An example cites the iHRIS Manage human resources information system.

Covers recording health workers' training credentials and managing their activities, then begins the supply chain management category with tools for tracking stock levels and alerting facilities and district managers to shortages.

Describes further supply chain interventions, including remote temperature monitoring of vaccines in the cold chain, registration of approved medicines and procurement management. It also covers reporting of falsified or substandard medicines and public health event notification, with an example of alerts for new multidrug-resistant or Rift Valley fever cases.

Describes the civil registration and vital statistics category, including digital notification, registration and certification of births and deaths, with an example of mobile reporting of events outside health facilities. It also begins health financing interventions, such as verifying health coverage membership.

Describes health financing interventions such as electronic insurance claims processing, performance-based payments to facilities through mobile money and budget planning tools. Examples include an electronic claims system and a web-based tool for tracking funds.

Covers determining subsidy levels for health coverage schemes and collecting insurance contributions by mobile payment, with an example from Kenya's national hospital insurance fund. It then introduces equipment and asset management, including tracking regulation of medical devices.

Describes health facility management interventions, such as master lists of facilities with unique identifiers and facility assessments, with an example of a portal of over 200 000 verified public health facilities.
Describes person-centred health certificate management, covering creating, validating, revoking and updating certificates such as digital vaccination certificates.
Introduces the group of digital health interventions for data services, aimed at optimal data management, use and governance.

A one-page overview of the data services interventions, listing data management, data coding, geospatial information management, data exchange and interoperability, and data governance compliance with their subcategories.

Describes data management interventions, including electronic data collection forms, data storage and aggregation, and data synthesis and visualization. It cites survey tools such as OpenDataKit and notes where further examples can be found online.

Covers automated data analysis to generate predictions, including artificial intelligence, with an example of predictive models for labour complications. It then describes data coding interventions, such as converting unstructured data into structured data, merging and deduplicating records and classifying disease codes.

Describes geospatial information management, including mapping health facilities, households, health events, people and providers. Examples include a facility map portal and an SMS-based outbreak alert dashboard.

Describes data exchange and interoperability interventions, including point-to-point integration, standards-based interoperability and message routing, with an example of a national health information exchange platform.
Describes data governance compliance interventions, including authentication and authorization, data protection, consent management and data provenance, and trust architecture for digital identities.

Introduces the types of digital services and applications in the classification, defined as the software, ICT systems and channels that deliver digital health interventions. It lists the five groupings, from point-of-service systems to registries and directories, with their numbered subtypes.

Defines point-of-service systems and describes their subtypes, such as communication systems, community-based information systems, decision support systems and diagnostic information systems. Each entry gives other descriptors and functional areas.

Continues defining point-of-service systems, including electronic medical records, laboratory information systems, personal health records, pharmacy information systems and telehealth systems, with their functional areas.
Defines health system and provider management systems, such as blood bank information systems and health financing information systems, with descriptors and functional areas.

Describes further management systems, including human resource information systems, learning and training systems and logistics management information systems, ending with research information systems.
Defines registries and directories, such as census and population information systems, civil registration and vital statistics systems and facility registries, with their functional areas.
Describes further registries and directories, including health worker registries, identity registries, immunization information systems, product catalogues and terminology and classification systems.
Defines data management services, such as analytics systems, data exchange and interoperability layers and environmental information systems, with descriptors and functional areas.
Describes further data management services, including geographic information systems, health management information systems, knowledge management systems and shared health records.

Defines surveillance and response systems, including emergency preparedness and response systems and public health and disease surveillance systems, with functions such as contact tracing and case notification.

The start of the reference list for the definitions and examples of digital health interventions, citing mainly entries in the mHealth Compendium database and literature on tailored health communication.

Continuation of the reference list for digital health intervention examples, citing a WHO global eHealth survey report, studies on body sensor networks and teledermatology and many mHealth Compendium entries.
Continuation of the reference list, citing mHealth Compendium entries, a WHO case study on emergency supply management software and WHO material on civil registration and vital statistics.

The end of the reference list, citing an ISO interoperability standard and a consent management study, followed by references for the service and application types such as the WHO digital implementation investment guide.
The annex divider page, carrying only the word 'Annex'.

Explains how the classification was developed: the first edition (2018) built on earlier mHealth classifications and WHO technical consultations, and the second edition used a collaborative, systematic public review. It gives links for submitting feedback and viewing the full list of examples.
A blank page with no extracted text.
A blank page with no extracted text.
